title: 3.4.16 Lab: Rewrite 3 Named Functions as Arrows
description: Convert three function declarations into one-line arrow expressions and confirm each still behaves the same. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the three declarations
steps.instructions: Define three separate function declarations, each with a different job: for example one that returns a number, one that returns a true/false answer, and one that returns a string. Use the function name() {} form.

steps.title: Convert each to an arrow
steps.instructions: Rewrite each declaration as a const assigned a one-line arrow function, using implicit return. Keep the same parameters and the same returned value as the declaration it replaces. Give each arrow a new name; reusing a declaration's name in the same file is a SyntaxError.

steps.title: Call all three and log results
steps.instructions: Call each of the three arrows with sample arguments and log the results with console.log. Check each result is what the original declaration would have returned.

requirements.title: Three arrow functions
requirements.description: At least three const variables are assigned arrow functions. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Each arrow is a const with a name, an equals sign, its parameters, =>, then the body. You need three of them.

requirements.title: Implicit return used
requirements.description: An arrow body is a bare expression with no opening brace. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Drop the braces and the word return. The one expression after => is returned for you.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: all three results are printed
requirements.description: At least three values are printed, and they are not all the same. Help: 3.4.8 (Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Call each of the three arrows and print every result. Printing the three results on one line, separated by commas, is fine.

checks.fail: Print the result of each of your three arrows (one console.log each, or all three in one). Three different jobs should give different results.
